members.note: Non-virtual, one caller in the game. It returns whether the ability was triggered; the component's own Trigger()/DoTrigger() body runs behind it, which is why the action reports the bool and reads the machine back instead of claiming the effect.

rows.ruling: ruling 88 restates the design's reshaping into state_request and deletes position/expiry_tick/evidence_kind
rows.reason: The row's ruled shape is forge.action.enemy.state_request: the native behaviour machine is entered by EnemyBehaviour.ChangeState(EB_States), and it takes a lease recipient the reshaped investigate never had. That row already exists in the catalog and is owned by the enemy control family, whose implementation reports it unregistered because no provider can mint or read the lease handle the runtime's handle pool owns. Declaring an investigate row here would either duplicate that row under a second id or advertise a position/evidence_kind request the game cannot carry, so nothing is declared.
rows.evidence: ForgeEnemy/Native/EnemyControlActions.cs (the module's own note on state_request) and ForgeEnemy/Native/EnemyControlContract.cs

rows.reason: no waypoint-path entry point exists: forge.resource.path has no producer (ruling 83) and the behaviour machine picks its own nodes; AIG_CourseNode carries no author-supplied path
EB_States and ES_StateEnum have no flee member (29 and 34 members, verified in the interop enums), and EnemyBehaviourData.WantsToFlee is a field the behaviour states read, not a request entry point
EnemyDetection keeps detection accumulation only (m_biggestDetectionBuildup, m_noiseDetection*); there is no threat table, no per-source hate value and no decay

inFlightLedger.lifecycle: Written when a submission is confirmed and the machine reports the component still running; dropped when AbilityIsDone() is true, when the enemy dies or despawns (ForgetBehavior), when the interruption path takes it (TakeRunningBehavior) and when the world changes (ClearBehaviors, wired into ClearWorld by the integration fragment).
inFlightLedger.noExpiry: No duration, timer or tick budget is attached. No native member gives an ability a duration, so the kernel's per-tick module hook (RuntimeModule.OnTick, batch-1) is not used by this slice and no double for it is needed.
inFlightLedger.handle: No capability row in this slice declares a handle port, and the kernel's handle pool is not reachable from a provider in the current tree (RuntimeKernel.CreateHandle is private and RuntimeModuleHandle exposes only Publish/CancelScope/Dispose). The ledger therefore keys rows by the enemy life rather than by a forged handle, and no second handle namespace is invented.
